# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chang_2023_rifapentine_mouse"))$reference`
* Rifapentine model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chang_2023_rifapentine_mouse"))$description`
* Rifabutin model: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Chang_2023_rifabutin_mouse"))$description`
* Article: [Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2023;67(7):e00481-23](https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00481-23)
  (open access, PMC10353356, with supplemental material)

Chang et al. used oral dosing of rifapentine (RPT) and rifabutin (RFB) in
mice to mimic the plasma exposure profiles that a long-acting injectable (LAI)
formulation might produce, and measured the bactericidal activity of those
profiles in a paucibacillary mouse model of tuberculosis preventive therapy.
Every PK analysis in the paper uses the same structure -- a one-compartment
model with first-order absorption, parameterised as CL/F, V/F and Ka -- fitted
separately to each dose group or regimen. The second PK/PD study, which ran for
8 weeks, added a time-dependent increase in CL/F that the authors attribute to
rifamycin autoinduction:

$$CL/F_{\mathrm{day}\,n} = (CL/F)_{\mathrm{day}\,1} \times (1 + \mathrm{Ind\_Factor})^{n-1}$$

The two packaged models carry that full structure, one per drug, with the
second-study fits as their default values. The pilot and first-study fits are
the same model with the induction factor absent, so this vignette reproduces
them by overriding the `ini()` values and setting `cl_time_fday = 0`.

# Population

All animals were BALB/c mice from Charles River Laboratories, dosed by oral
gavage in 0.2 mL with doses computed for an average body mass of 20 g.

* **Pilot PK study** (Table 1, Table S2). 84 female and 48 male uninfected
  mice, 8-10 weeks old, 12 per dose group. Rifapentine 0.1, 0.3, 1 and
  3 mg/kg and rifabutin 0.3, 1 and 3 mg/kg once daily in females (0.3 and
  3 mg/kg of each drug in males), Monday to Friday in week 1 and Monday to
  Thursday in week 2 (nine doses). Staggered mandibular bleeds at 0, 0.5, 1,
  2, 4, 6, 9 and 24 h after the first (day 0) and ninth (day 10) dose.
* **PK/PD study 1** (Tables 2-3, Figs. S3 and S5). 125 female mice in the
  paucibacillary model (rBCG30 immunization, M. tuberculosis H37Rv challenge,
  treatment 7 weeks later). Twice-daily (BID) regimens designed to hold the
  plasma trough or average concentration at a target, 7 days per week for
  3 weeks; every rifapentine regimen started with a loading dose.
* **PK/PD study 2** (Tables 4-5, Table S5, Fig. 2, Fig. S7). 147 female
  mice in the same model. Twice-daily oral doses changed every 4 days over
  8 weeks to trace the rise and slow decline of a simulated LAI injection
  (one simulated injection, or two given 4 weeks apart).

All fits pooled the individual mouse concentrations naively and minimised
least squares weighted by 1/(predicted)^2 (R 4.0.3, `pracma::lsqnonlin`), so
the models carry no between-subject variability and the residual magnitude
was not reported. The same information is stored in the `population` metadata
of each model.

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 1-compartment, first-order absorption, CL/F, V/F, Ka | -- | Methods, PK and PK/PD analyses |
| Induction equation `CL/F(day n) = CL/F(day 1) x (1 + Ind_Factor)^(n - 1)` | -- | Methods (equation image m001) |
| Day index: dosing day n - 1 = `floor(t / 24)` | -- | Table 4 footnote b and Methods: all regimens dosed 7 days per week from day 0 |
| RPT `lka` | log(0.42) | Table 5, LAI target 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses |
| RPT `lcl` | log(0.02) | Table 5, LAI target 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses |
| RPT `lvc` | log(0.35) | Table 5, LAI target 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses |
| RPT `cl_time_fday` | 0.011 | Table 5, LAI target 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses (Ind_Factor 1.1%) |
| RFB `lka` | log(10.03) | Table 5, LAI target 0.15 ug/mL, 1 dose |
| RFB `lcl` | log(1.06) | Table 5, LAI target 0.15 ug/mL, 1 dose |
| RFB `lvc` | log(13.23) | Table 5, LAI target 0.15 ug/mL, 1 dose |
| RFB `cl_time_fday` | 0.009 | Table 5, LAI target 0.15 ug/mL, 1 dose (Ind_Factor 0.9%) |
| `propSd` (both) | fixed(0) | Methods: 1/pred^2 weighting; magnitude not reported |
| Other study-2 regimen fits | see below | Table 5 |
| Pilot fits, female | see below | Table 1 |
| Pilot fits, male | see below | Table S2 |
| Study-1 fits | see below | Fig. S3 (RPT) and Fig. S5 (RFB) panel tables |
| Study-2 dosing schedules | see below | Table S5 |

The rifapentine default is the "LAI target 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses" fit because it
has the lowest relative standard error on every parameter of the five
rifapentine regimens; rifabutin has a single fitted study-2 regimen.

```{r models}
mod_rpt <- readModelDb("Chang_2023_rifapentine_mouse")
mod_rfb <- readModelDb("Chang_2023_rifabutin_mouse")
mods <- list(RPT = mod_rpt, RFB = mod_rfb)

# Solve one regimen with a given set of parameter estimates; Cc is the
# typical-value prediction (the models carry no random effects).
solve_fit <- function(drug, cl, v, ka, fday, events) {
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(
    mods[[drug]],
    events,
    params = c(lcl = log(cl), lvc = log(v), lka = log(ka), cl_time_fday = fday),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  )
  out[!duplicated(out$time), c("time", "Cc")]
}

trap_auc <- function(time, conc) {
  sum(diff(time) * (head(conc, -1) + tail(conc, -1)) / 2)
}
```

# Pilot PK study (Table 1 and Table S2)

Each pilot dose group was fitted separately with no induction term, to the
day-0 and day-10 data together (the Fig. S3 caption describes the pilot model as
fitted "including Day 10 PK data"; Table 1 and Table S2 print one parameter
set per dose group). The simulation below reproduces the pilot schedule -- nine
once-daily doses on days 0-4 and 7-10 -- with each group's own fit and runs
PKNCA on the 24-h interval after the first (day 0) and ninth (day 10) dose. The
reference values are the paper's observed Cmax and AUC0-24 from the
naive-pooled data, so the comparison is "fitted model versus data".

```{r pilot-fits}
pilot <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~sex,     ~dose, ~cl,   ~v,    ~ka,
  "RPT", "female", 0.1,   0.024, 0.743, 2.57,
  "RPT", "female", 0.3,   0.029, 0.736, 1.75,
  "RPT", "female", 1,     0.021, 0.643, 1.64,
  "RPT", "female", 3,     0.016, 0.418, 1.33,
  "RFB", "female", 0.3,   0.674, 7.360, 49.10,
  "RFB", "female", 1,     1.040, 7.490, 16.40,
  "RFB", "female", 3,     1.170, 8.670, 8.48,
  "RPT", "male",   0.3,   0.020, 0.449, 1.05,
  "RPT", "male",   3,     0.015, 0.287, 0.75,
  "RFB", "male",   0.3,   1.39,  9.87,  48.9,
  "RFB", "male",   3,     1.79,  11.0,  47.7
) |>
  mutate(group = sprintf("%s %s mg/kg (%s)", drug, dose, sex))

# Observed NCA, Table 1 (female) and Table S2 (male): day 0 then day 10.
pilot_ref <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,                   ~day, ~cmax,  ~auclast,
  "RPT 0.1 mg/kg (female)", 0,    0.130,  2.5,
  "RPT 0.1 mg/kg (female)", 10,   0.199,  3.6,
  "RPT 0.3 mg/kg (female)", 0,    0.386,  6.4,
  "RPT 0.3 mg/kg (female)", 10,   0.644,  9.6,
  "RPT 1 mg/kg (female)",   0,    1.580,  23.9,
  "RPT 1 mg/kg (female)",   10,   2.370,  38.7,
  "RPT 3 mg/kg (female)",   0,    6.690,  105.7,
  "RPT 3 mg/kg (female)",   10,   11.900, 166.6,
  "RFB 0.3 mg/kg (female)", 0,    0.053,  0.4,
  "RFB 0.3 mg/kg (female)", 10,   0.041,  0.3,
  "RFB 1 mg/kg (female)",   0,    0.140,  1.0,
  "RFB 1 mg/kg (female)",   10,   0.105,  0.8,
  "RFB 3 mg/kg (female)",   0,    0.325,  2.7,
  "RFB 3 mg/kg (female)",   10,   0.348,  2.4,
  "RPT 0.3 mg/kg (male)",   0,    0.491,  6.7,
  "RPT 0.3 mg/kg (male)",   10,   0.768,  10.5,
  "RPT 3 mg/kg (male)",     0,    10.6,   118.2,
  "RPT 3 mg/kg (male)",     10,   7.87,   159.8,
  "RFB 0.3 mg/kg (male)",   0,    0.034,  0.2,
  "RFB 0.3 mg/kg (male)",   10,   0.027,  0.2,
  "RFB 3 mg/kg (male)",     0,    0.299,  1.8,
  "RFB 3 mg/kg (male)",     10,   0.243,  1.6
) |>
  mutate(treatment = sprintf("%s, day %d", group, day))

pilot_dose_days <- c(0:4, 7:10)
sampling_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 24)

pilot_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(pilot)), function(i) {
  r <- pilot[i, ]
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = r$dose, cmt = "depot", time = pilot_dose_days * 24) |>
    rxode2::et(c(sampling_times, 240 + sampling_times), cmt = "central")
  s <- solve_fit(r$drug, r$cl, r$v, r$ka, 0, ev)
  bind_rows(
    mutate(filter(s, time <= 24), day = 0L),
    mutate(filter(s, time >= 240, time <= 264), day = 10L, time = time - 240)
  ) |>
    mutate(group = r$group, treatment = sprintf("%s, day %d", r$group, day), id = i)
}))
```

```{r pilot-nca}
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(
  dplyr::filter(pilot_sim, !is.na(Cc)),
  Cc ~ time | treatment + id
)
dose_df <- pilot_sim |>
  distinct(treatment, id) |>
  left_join(distinct(pilot_sim, treatment, group), by = "treatment") |>
  left_join(select(pilot, group, dose), by = "group") |>
  mutate(time = 0)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

pilot_cmp <- ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res,
  as.data.frame(select(pilot_ref, treatment, cmax, auclast)),
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "auclast"),
  tolerance_pct = 30,
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", auclast = "ug*h/mL")
)
knitr::kable(pilot_cmp, caption = "Pilot study Cmax and AUC0-24 after the day-0 and day-10 doses: simulated from each dose group's own fit (Table 1 / Table S2) versus the paper's observed values.")
```

```{r pilot-check}
pilot_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "auclast")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, sim = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(
    pivot_longer(select(pilot_ref, treatment, cmax, auclast), -treatment,
      names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"
    ),
    by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - ref) / ref)
pilot_auc <- filter(pilot_nca, PPTESTCD == "auclast")
pilot_auc_female <- filter(pilot_auc, grepl("female", treatment))
stopifnot(
  nrow(pilot_nca) == 2 * nrow(pilot_ref),
  # Centre: a mis-transcribed CL/F or V/F moves a group by tens of percent.
  abs(median(pilot_nca$pct_diff)) < 10,
  median(abs(pilot_auc$pct_diff)) < 15,
  # Envelope over the main-text (Table 1, female) groups.
  quantile(abs(pilot_auc_female$pct_diff), 0.9) < 25
)
```

Simulating the whole nine-dose schedule reproduces the day-0 to day-10 rise in
rifapentine exposure that the Results describe (Cmax and AUC0-24 about 1.5- to
1.6-fold higher on day 10): with half-lives of 18-21 h and once-daily dosing,
rifapentine accumulates, so a single time-invariant fit per group spans both
days. For the Table 1 (female) groups the fitted AUC0-24 is within 20% of the
observed value in all but one interval. The exceptions, all visible in the
table above, are properties of the published fits rather than of the
implementation:

* RFB 0.3 mg/kg (female), day 10: the observed AUC0-24 of 0.3 ug*h/mL is near
  the 0.05 ug/mL limit of quantification, while the same fit matches day 0.
  The day-0 Cmax of that group is also below the observed value, because with
  Ka near 50 1/h the fitted curve peaks before the first 0.5-h sample.
* RPT 0.3 mg/kg (male): the Table S2 fit (CL/F 0.020 L/h/kg, V/F 0.449 L/kg,
  Ka 1.05 1/h) gives about 40% more AUC0-24 than observed on both days. The
  printed half-life of 15.6 h equals 0.693 x V/F / CL/F, so the three printed
  values are mutually consistent and there is no single-value transcription
  error to correct; the fit simply does not reproduce the reported NCA.
* RPT 3 mg/kg (male), day 10: observed Cmax (7.87 ug/mL) is lower than on
  day 0 (10.6 ug/mL) with a Tmax of 9 h, a profile a one-compartment
  first-order absorption model cannot follow.

# PK/PD study 1: steady target concentrations (Table 3, Figs. S3 and S5)

Twice-daily doses were given at 7 am and 5 pm (10 h and 14 h apart; Fig. S2
caption), and the rifapentine regimens opened with a loading dose in place of
the first maintenance dose. Each regimen's fitted CL/F, V/F and Ka are printed
beneath its panel in Fig. S3 (rifapentine) or Fig. S5 (rifabutin). Table 3
reports the average and trough concentrations of each fitted curve, which the
simulation below recomputes over day 19 (the last full day before week 3).

```{r study1}
study1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~regimen,              ~load, ~maint, ~cl,  ~v,    ~ka,   ~cave_ref, ~ctrough_ref,
  "RPT", "RPT 0.075 mg/kg BID", 0.2,   0.075,  0.03, 1.47,  0.89,  0.20,      0.17,
  "RPT", "RPT 0.25 mg/kg BID",  0.625, 0.25,   0.03, 1.10,  1.01,  0.63,      0.54,
  "RPT", "RPT 0.75 mg/kg BID",  1.875, 0.75,   0.02, 0.88,  1.33,  2.98,      2.60,
  "RPT", "RPT 1.25 mg/kg BID",  3.125, 1.25,   0.02, 0.68,  0.81,  5.60,      4.90,
  "RFB", "RFB 0.75 mg/kg BID",  NA,    0.75,   0.77, 8.12,  25.33, 0.09,      0.04,
  "RFB", "RFB 1.5 mg/kg BID",   NA,    1.5,    0.88, 8.74,  23.40, 0.16,      0.07,
  "RFB", "RFB 2.5 mg/kg BID",   NA,    2.5,    0.93, 10.97, 25.23, 0.24,      0.12,
  "RFB", "RFB 5.5 mg/kg BID",   NA,    5.5,    0.86, 8.56,  24.09, 0.60,      0.25
)

bid_times <- sort(c((0:20) * 24, (0:20) * 24 + 10))

study1_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(study1)), function(i) {
  r <- study1[i, ]
  amt <- rep(r$maint, length(bid_times))
  if (!is.na(r$load)) amt[1] <- r$load
  ev <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1, time = bid_times, amt = amt, evid = 1, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(id = 1, time = seq(0, 21 * 24, by = 0.1), amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
  solve_fit(r$drug, r$cl, r$v, r$ka, 0, ev) |>
    mutate(regimen = r$regimen, drug = r$drug)
}))

study1_cmp <- study1_sim |>
  filter(time >= 19 * 24, time <= 20 * 24) |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(cave_sim = trap_auc(time, Cc) / 24, ctrough_sim = min(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(study1, by = "regimen") |>
  mutate(
    cave_pct = 100 * (cave_sim - cave_ref) / cave_ref,
    ctrough_pct = 100 * (ctrough_sim - ctrough_ref) / ctrough_ref
  )

study1_cmp |>
  arrange(match(regimen, study1$regimen)) |>
  transmute(
    Regimen = regimen,
    `Cave, Table 3 (ug/mL)` = cave_ref,
    `Cave, simulated` = signif(cave_sim, 3),
    `Cave % diff` = round(cave_pct, 1),
    `Ctrough, Table 3 (ug/mL)` = ctrough_ref,
    `Ctrough, simulated` = signif(ctrough_sim, 3),
    `Ctrough % diff` = round(ctrough_pct, 1)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Average and trough concentrations of the study-1 fitted curves (Table 3) versus simulation with each regimen's Fig. S3 / Fig. S5 estimates.")

stopifnot(
  nrow(study1_cmp) == nrow(study1),
  abs(median(c(study1_cmp$cave_pct, study1_cmp$ctrough_pct))) < 10,
  max(abs(study1_cmp$cave_pct)) < 15,
  max(abs(study1_cmp$ctrough_pct)) < 15
)
```

Every average and trough concentration agrees within 15%. The residual
differences are the size expected from the two-significant-figure CL/F values
printed in Figs. S3 and S5 (for example, a printed rifapentine CL/F of 0.03
L/h/kg covers 0.025-0.035): the steady-state average concentration is the
daily dose divided by 24 x CL/F, so it moves one-for-one with the rounding.

```{r study1-plot, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(study1_sim, aes(time / (24 * 7), Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "orange") +
  geom_hline(
    data = study1, aes(yintercept = ctrough_ref), colour = "red", linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Weeks of dosing", y = "Plasma concentration (ug/mL)",
    title = "Study-1 fitted profiles (replicates the yellow curves of Figs. S3 and S5)",
    caption = "Dashed red line: fitted trough concentration from Table 3."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PK/PD study 2: simulated LAI profiles (Fig. 2, Table 5)

Table S5 lists the twice-daily dose for each of the 14 four-day periods of the
8-week course. The total doses it implies equal the Table 5 totals (35.4, 61.8,
74.0, 129.2 and 113.8 mg/kg for rifapentine; 254.8 mg/kg for the rifabutin
regimen), which confirms the schedule is transcribed correctly. The two daily
doses are placed 10 h and 14 h apart as in study 1. Each regimen is solved with
its own Table 5 fit, including its induction factor.

```{r study2-schedule}
table_s5 <- list(
  "RPT LAI 0.6 ug/mL, 1 dose" = c(0.75, 0.6, 0.5, 0.45, 0.375, 0.325, 0.275, 0.24, 0.21, 0.18, 0.16, 0.14, 0.12, 0.1),
  "RPT LAI 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses" = c(0.75, 0.6, 0.5, 0.45, 0.375, 0.325, 0.275, 1, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.52, 0.45, 0.375),
  "RPT LAI 2 ug/mL, 1 dose" = c(1.6, 1.2, 1.1, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.425, 0.375, 0.325, 0.275, 0.25, 0.2),
  "RPT LAI 2 ug/mL, 2 doses" = c(1.6, 1.2, 1.1, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 2.1, 1.625, 1.475, 1.225, 1.075, 0.95, 0.8),
  "RPT LAI 3.5 ug/mL, 1 dose" = c(2.4, 1.9, 1.6, 1.4, 1.2, 1.1, 0.875, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5, 0.45, 0.375, 0.325),
  "RFB LAI 0.15 ug/mL, 1 dose" = c(5, 4, 3.5, 3, 2.75, 2.5, 2.2, 2, 1.6, 1.4, 1.2, 1, 0.9, 0.8)
)

study2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,                     ~drug, ~cl,  ~v,    ~ka,   ~fday, ~total_ref, ~auc_ref, ~tr28_ref, ~tr52_ref,
  "RPT LAI 0.6 ug/mL, 1 dose",  "RPT", 0.02, 0.37,  0.23,  0.011, 35.4,       1320,     0.60,      0.15,
  "RPT LAI 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses", "RPT", 0.02, 0.35,  0.42,  0.011, 61.8,       2093,     0.52,      0.45,
  "RPT LAI 2 ug/mL, 1 dose",    "RPT", 0.02, 0.64,  5.09,  0.011, 74.0,       3251,     1.58,      0.38,
  "RPT LAI 2 ug/mL, 2 doses",   "RPT", 0.02, 0.48,  0.62,  0.012, 129.2,      5074,     1.52,      1.37,
  "RPT LAI 3.5 ug/mL, 1 dose",  "RPT", 0.02, 0.45,  0.57,  0.011, 113.8,      5217,     2.32,      0.59,
  "RFB LAI 0.15 ug/mL, 1 dose", "RFB", 1.06, 13.23, 10.03, 0.009, 254.8,      200,      0.06,      0.02
)

study2$total_s5 <- vapply(study2$regimen, function(r) 8 * sum(table_s5[[r]]), numeric(1))
stopifnot(all(abs(study2$total_s5 - study2$total_ref) < 0.05))

study2_events <- function(regimen) {
  day_dose <- rep(table_s5[[regimen]], each = 4) # 14 periods x 4 days = 56 days
  am <- (0:55) * 24
  bind_rows(
    data.frame(id = 1, time = c(am, am + 10), amt = rep(day_dose, 2), evid = 1, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(
      id = 1, time = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 56 * 24, by = 0.25), 28 * 24, 52 * 24))),
      amt = 0, evid = 0, cmt = "central"
    )
  ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
}

study2_sim <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(study2)), function(i) {
  r <- study2[i, ]
  solve_fit(r$drug, r$cl, r$v, r$ka, r$fday, study2_events(r$regimen)) |>
    mutate(regimen = r$regimen)
}))
```

```{r fig2, fig.height = 7}
study2_sim |>
  filter(grepl("^RPT", regimen)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / (24 * 7), Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "orange") +
  facet_wrap(~regimen, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:8) +
  labs(
    x = "Weeks of dosing", y = "Plasma concentration (ug/mL)",
    title = "Rifapentine simulated-LAI regimens (replicates the yellow curves of Fig. 2A-E)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r figS7, fig.height = 3.5}
study2_sim |>
  filter(grepl("^RFB", regimen)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / (24 * 7), Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "orange") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, colour = "grey50", linetype = "dotted") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:8) +
  labs(
    x = "Weeks of dosing", y = "Plasma concentration (ug/mL)",
    title = "Rifabutin LAI target 0.15 ug/mL (replicates the yellow curve of Fig. S7D)",
    caption = "Dotted line: rifabutin LLOQ 0.05 ug/mL."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Cumulative AUC and troughs (Table 5)

Table 5 reports, for each regimen, the cumulative AUC of the fitted curve over
the 8-week course and the fitted trough concentration on days 28 and 52 (taken
here as the pre-morning-dose concentration on those days).

```{r table5}
study2_cmp <- study2_sim |>
  group_by(regimen) |>
  summarise(
    auc_sim = trap_auc(time, Cc),
    tr28_sim = Cc[time == 28 * 24][1],
    tr52_sim = Cc[time == 52 * 24][1],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  inner_join(study2, by = "regimen") |>
  arrange(match(regimen, study2$regimen)) |>
  mutate(auc_pct = 100 * (auc_sim - auc_ref) / auc_ref)

study2_cmp |>
  transmute(
    Regimen = regimen,
    `Cum. AUC, Table 5 (ug*h/mL)` = auc_ref,
    `Cum. AUC, simulated` = round(auc_sim),
    `AUC % diff` = round(auc_pct, 1),
    `Day 28 trough, Table 5` = tr28_ref,
    `Day 28 trough, simulated` = signif(tr28_sim, 2),
    `Day 52 trough, Table 5` = tr52_ref,
    `Day 52 trough, simulated` = signif(tr52_sim, 2)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Fitted cumulative AUC (0-8 weeks) and troughs of the study-2 regimens: Table 5 versus simulation with each regimen's Table 5 estimates.")
```

The rifabutin regimen, whose CL/F is printed to three significant figures,
reproduces the published AUC within 2%. Every rifapentine CL/F in Table 5 is
printed as 0.02 L/h/kg -- one significant figure, compatible with any value
from 0.015 to 0.025 -- and the AUC scales almost inversely with CL/F, so the
rifapentine AUC differences of up to about 11% are rounding, not structure.
The check below makes this explicit: it back-solves, for each rifapentine
regimen, the day-1 CL/F that reproduces the published cumulative AUC with all
other parameters at their Table 5 values, and confirms that this CL/F rounds
to the printed 0.02.

```{r implied-cl}
auc_for_cl <- function(cl, r) {
  s <- solve_fit(r$drug, cl, r$v, r$ka, r$fday, study2_events(r$regimen))
  trap_auc(s$time, s$Cc)
}

implied <- filter(study2, drug == "RPT")
implied$cl_implied <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(implied)), function(i) {
  r <- implied[i, ]
  uniroot(function(cl) auc_for_cl(cl, r) - r$auc_ref, interval = c(0.01, 0.04), tol = 1e-6)$root
}, numeric(1))

implied |>
  transmute(
    Regimen = regimen,
    `CL/F printed (L/h/kg)` = cl,
    `CL/F reproducing the Table 5 AUC` = signif(cl_implied, 3)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Day-1 CL/F that reproduces each rifapentine regimen's published cumulative AUC.")

stopifnot(
  all(round(implied$cl_implied, 2) == 0.02),
  abs(study2_cmp$auc_pct[study2_cmp$drug == "RFB"]) < 5,
  abs(median(study2_cmp$auc_pct)) < 10
)
```

Every implied CL/F lies between 0.018 and 0.022 L/h/kg, inside the rounding
interval of the printed 0.02. The troughs follow the same pattern: they are
within the range spanned by CL/F 0.015-0.025 but, being single-time-point
values on a steep part of the curve, they are more sensitive to the rounding
than the AUC is.

## Induction factor

```{r induction}
fold_day52 <- c(RPT = 1.011^51, RFB = 1.009^51)
fold_day52
stopifnot(all(abs(fold_day52 - c(1.75, 1.58)) < 0.01))
```

With CL/F on dosing day 52 equal to CL/F on day 1 times (1 + Ind_Factor)^51,
the rifapentine factor of 1.1% per day gives a 1.75-fold higher clearance by
day 52 and the rifabutin factor of 0.9% a 1.58-fold higher clearance,
consistent with the Results' "~1.7 times higher clearance by day 52 of the
study than day 1".

# Pharmacodynamic summary (not encoded)

The paper summarises each regimen's lung CFU time course with a "net bacterial
elimination" rate constant, knet, estimated as the slope of a straight line
through log10 CFU versus time (Methods; Table 3). These are per-arm
descriptive slopes with no fitted exposure-response function linking them to
concentration (Fig. S4 plots them against dose and exposure only), so they are
reported here for reference rather than encoded as a PD model.

| Study-1 regimen | knet (1/week) [% RSE] | Initial log10 CFU/lung |
|---|---|---|
| Untreated | 0.05 [124] | 4.45 |
| Rifampin 10 mg/kg QD | -0.21 [32.88] | 4.45 |
| RPT 0.075 mg/kg BID | 0.12 [56.71] | 4.46 |
| RPT 0.25 mg/kg BID | 0.07 [98.28] | 4.44 |
| RPT 0.75 mg/kg BID | -0.22 [29.30] | 4.44 |
| RPT 1.25 mg/kg BID | -0.28 [23.20] | 4.45 |
| RFB 0.75 mg/kg BID | -0.09 [90.11] | 4.46 |
| RFB 1.5 mg/kg BID | -0.20 [39.48] | 4.46 |
| RFB 2.5 mg/kg BID | -0.30 [25.41] | 4.45 |
| RFB 5.5 mg/kg BID | -0.48 [15.86] | 4.45 |

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Many fits, one structure.** The paper fits its one-compartment model
  separately to 25 dose groups and regimens. The packaged models carry the
  second-study structure (with the induction term) and one fit as defaults;
  every other fit is listed in the model file comments and reproduced here by
  overriding the `ini()` values, with `cl_time_fday = 0` for the pilot and
  study-1 fits, which had no induction term.
* **Choice of rifapentine defaults.** The "LAI target 0.6 ug/mL, 2 doses"
  regimen was chosen because its estimates have the lowest relative standard
  errors of the five rifapentine regimens. CL/F (0.02) and Ind_Factor (1.1%)
  are the same, to the printed precision, in four of the five regimens; V/F and
  Ka vary more between regimens and are poorly determined in some (V/F RSE
  122%, Ka RSE 129% for the single-dose 0.6 ug/mL regimen).
* **Day index.** The induction equation counts dosing days. All study-2
  regimens were dosed every day from day 0, so dosing day n - 1 is
  `floor(t / 24)` with `t = 0` at the first dose. A user simulating a schedule
  with dosing-free days, or a first dose away from `t = 0`, must account for
  this.
* **Residual error.** The fits minimised least squares weighted by
  1/(predicted)^2, which corresponds to a proportional error model, but no
  residual magnitude is reported; `propSd` is fixed at 0.
* **Near-zero RSE on Ka.** Several rifabutin Ka estimates (and one
  rifapentine estimate, 5.09 1/h with an RSE of 0.004%) carry an RSE of about
  0%. The paper never states that a parameter was fixed; the authors describe
  rifabutin absorption as very rapid at every dose, so the near-zero RSE
  reflects an absorption rate the 0.5-1 h earliest samples cannot inform. These
  values are treated as estimates, not fixed values.
* **Dose timing.** Twice-daily doses are placed 10 h and 14 h apart (7 am and
  5 pm), as stated for study 1 in the Fig. S2 caption; the Methods give
  12 +/- 2 h for both studies. The cumulative AUC and average concentration are
  insensitive to this choice.
* **AUC window and trough day.** Table 5 does not state the integration window
  of the "cumulative AUC"; the full 8-week (56-day) course is used. The day-28
  and day-52 troughs are read at the pre-morning-dose time on those study days.
* **Body weight.** Doses and parameters are per kilogram; the paper dosed for
  an average mouse of 20 g and reports no weight effect.
* **Rifabutin "LAI target 0.045 ug/mL" regimen.** Not fitted by the authors
  (truncated PK profile, most samples below the LLOQ; Table 5 footnote f), so
  it has no parameter set to reproduce.
